project.name: easy-for-net
conventions: Features are isolated vertical slices: a type under Features/X never references a type under Features/Y unless that type is marked [AllowOutside]. Cross-feature access goes through a service interface, never through another feature's entities — the architecture tests fail the gate otherwise.

One endpoint is one file: the Endpoint, its Request, Validator, Response/DTOs and the Mapperly mapper live together. Global usings live in Meta.cs, and every C# file opens with its file-scoped namespace, then a blank line, then its using directives.

A new permission is three edits that must agree: the constant in Permissions/Allow.cs, its definition in the feature's PermissionsProvider, and the mirror in src/frontend/web/allow.ts. A new feature (entitlement) is the same triple: FeatureNames.cs, the slice's FeaturesProvider, and feature-names.ts.

departments.label: Design
departments.why: Decides what the screen should be — layout, states, narrow widths, dark mode and RTL — before code makes that decision by accident.

departments.label: Data
departments.why: Entities, their EF configuration, migrations and seeding — a shape change invalidates queries, indexes and the seeder together.

departments.label: Backend
departments.why: Endpoints, services, permissions, feature management and their tests — everything behind the HTTP surface.

departments.label: Front end
departments.why: The Next.js app: locale-prefixed routes, RTK Query slices, forms, translations and the shared components.

departments.label: QA / acceptance
departments.why: Asks whether the brief was actually satisfied, not merely whether the build is green.

departments.label: Security
departments.why: Authentication, permissions, tenant isolation, plan gating and configuration are where a mistake is not local.

departments.label: UI / UX
departments.why: Layout, hierarchy and states are judged by eye, and nothing else in the loop looks.

departments.label: Code review
departments.why: Sees what a green gate cannot: a tenant filter missing, a permission unchecked, a test weakened to pass.

skills.why: The one-file layout, route group, permissions, validator and Mapperly mapper have an order that is easy to get half-right.
An entity change is not done until its configuration, DbSet and migration agree.
Test classes run in parallel against one database; a test that leans on state it did not create fails intermittently.
A permission lives in three places that must agree, plus the nav and route gating on the web.
A feature is declared in three places, and gating a permission on it has three callers that must not disagree.
Keys are shared across every locale file and three translator entry points.

skills.when: for a web API slice change
skills.why: Slices inject into the one shared appApi, and DTOs mirror the backend by name.

preflight.name: Postgres
preflight.whenMissing: start the PostgreSQL service — the backend tests and live checks need it, so every task fails its gate until it is up
